page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The reagent
lines: Phenol C₆H₅OH is reduced to benzene.
The vapour of phenol is passed over
The zinc removes the oxygen atom of
the –OH group and is left behind as
steps.why: Reduction here means the loss of oxygen: the hydroxyl group of phenol is replaced by a hydrogen atom and the oxygen leaves on the zinc as zinc oxide. Zinc dust is used because it is finely divided, so it reacts readily when heated.
common_mistakes: Using zinc in solution. The phenol vapour is passed over heated zinc dust.
Reducing the ring as well. Only the –OH group is removed, so the product is benzene and not cyclohexane.
steps.memory_tip: Phenol vapour over hot zinc dust: the oxygen leaves as ZnO and benzene remains.
steps.margin_note: Name the reagent as heated zinc dust before writing the equation.

steps.label: The equation
lines: Benzene C₆H₆ is the product and zinc
Atoms: 6 C, 6 H, 1 O and 1 Zn on
steps.why: Counting the atoms shows the equation is balanced as it stands: one zinc atom takes the one oxygen atom, and the six carbon and six hydrogen atoms pass through unchanged into benzene.
common_mistakes: Writing ZnO₂ or Zn(OH)₂ as the by-product. One zinc atom with one oxygen atom gives ZnO.
Adding hydrogen to balance. Phenol C₆H₅OH already carries the six hydrogen atoms that benzene needs.
steps.memory_tip: The zinc removes the oxygen as ZnO and the six hydrogen atoms stay on the ring.
steps.margin_note: One closing line naming benzene as the product completes the answer.

insider_note: The product here is benzene, not cyclohexane. Only the hydroxyl group is removed; the ring is left as it was.
